included: global catastrophic and continuity risks supported by public primary sources
leading indicators that an automated process can monitor
explicit authority boundaries and candidate owners
excluded: probabilistic forecasts not supplied by the cited sources
claims that risks have been reduced
outreach, spending, deployment, or operational intervention
scope.statement: This register is a decision-support artifact. Its existence is not evidence that any external risk has been reduced.

methodology.method: Qualitative, evidence-informed ordinal ranking. Higher ranks combine potential harm to life and continuity, current warning signals, cross-system reach, and the value of low-cost reversible monitoring. No unsupported numeric event probabilities are inferred.
limitations: The dimensions are not commensurable and the ordinal ranking is judgment-dependent.
The public sources differ in geographic coverage, reporting lag, definitions, and evidential strength.
Several risks interact, so ranks must not be read as independent probabilities or additive expected losses.
This first version uses one principal source per risk and requires periodic source expansion and adversarial review.
Candidate responses are research and preparedness options, not findings of effectiveness or authorization to act externally.

sources.title: Increasing focus on nuclear weapons amid heightened escalation risks — new SIPRI Yearbook out now
limitations: Warhead counts are estimates because nuclear-armed states disclose incomplete information.
The source describes arsenals and escalation conditions but does not assign an annual probability of nuclear use.

sources.title: International AI Safety Report 2026
limitations: AI capabilities and safeguards change faster than the assessment cycle.
The report identifies uneven evidence and substantial uncertainty, especially for severe loss-of-control scenarios.

sources.title: The changing face of pandemic risk: how we need to adapt, protect and connect
limitations: This strategic overview is not a pathogen-specific risk assessment or outbreak forecast.
Reported surveillance signals depend on unequal national detection and reporting capacity.

sources.title: State of the Global Climate 2025
limitations: Global indicators do not capture every local exposure, vulnerability, or adaptation difference.
Observed trends do not by themselves quantify the timing of specific tipping elements or future disasters.

sources.title: 2026 Global Report on Food Crises: Joint analysis for better decisions
sources.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
limitations: The report concentrates on countries and territories selected for food-crisis analysis rather than all food insecurity worldwide.
Access constraints and heterogeneous assessment coverage can produce revisions and undercounts.

sources.title: Thematic Assessment Report on the Interlinkages among Biodiversity, Water, Food and Health
sources.publisher: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
limitations: The global synthesis necessarily aggregates diverse regional conditions and knowledge systems.
The assessment establishes coupled trends and response options but not a single probability for nexus-wide collapse.

sources.title: Global Assessment Report 2025: Resilience Pays — Financing and Investing for our Future
sources.publisher: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction
limitations: Economic loss estimates rely on modeling and incomplete reporting, especially for indirect and non-market harms.
The global framing does not replace local multi-hazard and dependency analysis.

sources.title: Countering Chinese State-Sponsored Actors Compromise of Networks Worldwide to Feed Global Espionage System
limitations: The advisory covers a documented threat cluster, not the full distribution of infrastructure cyber risk.
Public indicators can lag active operations and are biased toward observed compromises.

sources.title: After Action Report: 2024 Space Weather Simulation Exercise
limitations: A simulation exercise tests coordination and assumptions; it is not evidence of actual system failure rates.
The exercise is United States-centered and cannot represent every international infrastructure dependency.

sources.title: UNESCO and its partners are building capacity to protect documentary heritage in the face of disasters
limitations: The article describes a regional capacity-building activity rather than measuring global archival loss prevalence.
Documentary heritage coverage does not encompass all tacit, scientific, software, or born-digital knowledge dependencies.

risks.title: Nuclear escalation, miscalculation, or arms-control failure
risks.rankingRationale: Immediate high-consequence potential, large deployed arsenals, high-alert forces, and eroding arms-control constraints give this risk the strongest combination of directive impact and urgency despite limited tractability for this program.

keyUnknowns: classified doctrine, command reliability, and actual readiness
the probability that regional conflict or false warning crosses nuclear thresholds

leadingIndicators.indicator: Changes in deployed and high-alert warhead estimates, arms-control participation, and public nuclear-use signaling
leadingIndicators.directionOfConcern: Rising deployed or high-alert totals, abandoned constraints, or more explicit use threats
leadingIndicators.updateCadence: quarterly signal scan and annual source refresh

reversibleResponses.action: Maintain a versioned public-source escalation dashboard and draft geographically diverse continuity options
reversibleResponses.trigger: A material adverse change in two monitored indicators or a new SIPRI assessment
reversibleResponses.rollback: Retire the dashboard version, preserve its evidence record, and restore the last verified indicator definitions
reversibleResponses.authorityBoundary: The automated body may monitor public data and draft bounded options. Any credentialed access, outreach, spending, physical action, or legal commitment requires a separately classified packet; human escalation is allowed only when a documented owner-only capability remains truly unautomatable.

risks.title: Advanced AI misuse, severe malfunction, or loss of control
risks.rankingRationale: Rapidly changing general-purpose capabilities can amplify cyber, biological, manipulation, and autonomy hazards. Consequences could be severe and safeguards remain incomplete, while uncertainty keeps the rank below the more directly observed nuclear condition.

keyUnknowns: future capability scaling and deployment concentration
real-world effectiveness and circumvention resistance of layered safeguards
likelihood and severity of loss-of-control pathways

leadingIndicators.indicator: Reported capability gains in high-risk domains alongside measured safeguard failures and autonomous operation
leadingIndicators.directionOfConcern: Capability improvement outpacing independent evaluations, incident reporting, and defense-in-depth
leadingIndicators.updateCadence: monthly evidence scan and on each international report update

reversibleResponses.action: Maintain an evidence-separated capability, incident, and safeguard registry with preregistered update criteria
reversibleResponses.trigger: A verified high-severity incident, a new dangerous capability evaluation, or material safeguard regression
reversibleResponses.rollback: Revert disputed classifications to unverified and preserve the challenged evidence and reviewer rationale
reversibleResponses.authorityBoundary: Automation may analyze public evidence, test local non-deployed controls, and prepare reviewable changes. It may not access restricted systems, release hazardous capability details, or deploy autonomous agents without a bounded authority assessment; humans are an exceptional escalation endpoint, not routine operators.

risks.title: Pandemic or other transboundary biological event
risks.rankingRationale: Recent emergence across multiple pathogen families, global connectivity, and uneven surveillance create high near-term preservation relevance. Monitoring and preparedness are comparatively tractable and reversible, raising information value.

keyUnknowns: undetected transmission where surveillance is weak
pathogen-specific severity, transmissibility, and countermeasure escape
public trust and equitable access to countermeasures

leadingIndicators.indicator: WHO notices of unusual clusters, sustained human-to-human transmission, geographic spread, and health-system stress
leadingIndicators.directionOfConcern: More sustained transmission, broader geography, greater severity, or declining response capacity
leadingIndicators.updateCadence: weekly public-health scan and event-driven refresh

reversibleResponses.action: Keep a pathogen-agnostic preparedness checklist and source-linked trigger matrix under version control
reversibleResponses.trigger: WHO reports sustained novel transmission or a relevant preparedness gap is independently verified
reversibleResponses.rollback: Archive superseded triggers and restore the last verified checklist if evidence is retracted
reversibleResponses.authorityBoundary: The automated body may monitor, model, and draft preparedness material from public sources. Medical guidance, biological experimentation, protected health data, procurement, and external coordination require separate authority and safety review; human escalation is reserved for a proven non-delegable decision.

risks.title: Compounding climate extremes and long-lived Earth-system change
risks.rankingRationale: Observed warming, record ocean heat, sea-level rise, and recurring extremes create persistent, geographically broad harm and amplify other risks. Some effects are already measured, though the most catastrophic thresholds and timing remain uncertain.

keyUnknowns: regional compound-event timing and adaptation performance
the timing and reversibility of specific tipping elements
future emissions and aerosol trajectories

leadingIndicators.indicator: Global temperature anomaly, ocean heat content, sea-level trend, ice loss, and compound extreme records
leadingIndicators.directionOfConcern: Persistent record values, accelerating trends, or correlated extremes across major producing and population regions
leadingIndicators.updateCadence: quarterly indicator update and annual WMO refresh

reversibleResponses.action: Map continuity-critical assets against public multi-hazard indicators and generate reversible adaptation experiments
reversibleResponses.trigger: A verified trend acceleration or repeated exposure of a critical dependency
reversibleResponses.rollback: Remove unsupported exposure links and reinstate the last independently reviewed map
reversibleResponses.authorityBoundary: Automated analysis and sandboxed simulations are autonomous. Changes to infrastructure, land, procurement, public claims, or third-party obligations need separately verified authority; escalate to a human only for an evidenced owner-only consent, legal, or physical constraint.

risks.title: Acute and compounding food-system shocks
risks.rankingRationale: Acute food insecurity is widespread and entwined with conflict, economic shocks, weather extremes, and displacement. The harm is current and cascading, with useful public indicators and reversible analytical preparedness options.

keyUnknowns: conditions in inaccessible or unassessed populations
joint effects of conflict, trade restrictions, input prices, and extreme weather
timeliness and durability of humanitarian access

leadingIndicators.indicator: Population in IPC/CH Phase 3 or above, famine classifications, price anomalies, and simultaneous production shocks
leadingIndicators.directionOfConcern: More affected people, higher severity phases, simultaneous breadbasket shocks, or constrained access
leadingIndicators.updateCadence: monthly situation scan and annual GRFC refresh

reversibleResponses.action: Build a public-data food dependency and correlated-shock map with explicit missing-data flags
reversibleResponses.trigger: A new famine classification, synchronized production anomaly, or major access deterioration
reversibleResponses.rollback: Quarantine unreliable feeds and restore the last verified dependency snapshot
reversibleResponses.authorityBoundary: Automation may assemble and test public-data maps. Aid allocation, market participation, outreach, and procurement are external actions requiring bounded authorization; a human is contacted only when automation proves it cannot obtain necessary consent or exercise a legally reserved authority.

risks.title: Coupled biodiversity, water, food, and health degradation
risks.rankingRationale: Interdependent ecological and social systems can transmit losses across health, water security, food production, and resilience. The slower, distributed dynamics lower immediate rank but raise systemic and irreversible downside.

keyUnknowns: local threshold behavior and delayed feedbacks
distributional effects and transferability of response options
interactions with climate, trade, land use, and emerging disease

leadingIndicators.indicator: Co-movement of biodiversity integrity, freshwater condition, nutrition, and zoonotic or health burden indicators
leadingIndicators.directionOfConcern: Concurrent deterioration across multiple nexus domains or response in one domain shifting harm to another
leadingIndicators.updateCadence: quarterly literature scan and on each IPBES assessment update

reversibleResponses.action: Create a cross-domain evidence graph that flags proposed responses with likely spillovers and unresolved tradeoffs
reversibleResponses.trigger: A candidate intervention affects two or more nexus domains or a shared threshold indicator deteriorates
reversibleResponses.rollback: Withdraw unsupported graph edges and preserve rejected hypotheses for later reassessment
reversibleResponses.authorityBoundary: The automated body may synthesize public evidence and challenge tradeoffs. Field intervention, access to protected ecological data, land-use decisions, or stakeholder commitments require separate authority; human involvement is exceptional and evidence-triggered.

risks.title: Cascading multi-hazard disaster and loss of financial resilience
risks.rankingRationale: Disasters propagate through debt, insurance, supply chains, ecosystems, and public capacity. These connections can turn otherwise bounded hazards into persistent continuity failures, while dependency mapping offers high information value at low reversible cost.

keyUnknowns: unreported indirect and non-market losses
cross-border propagation through opaque financial and supply networks
whether resilience investment reaches the most exposed systems

leadingIndicators.indicator: Growth in disaster losses, protection gaps, uninsurability, disaster-linked debt stress, and repeated service interruption
leadingIndicators.directionOfConcern: Losses and protection gaps rising faster than resilience investment or recovery capacity
leadingIndicators.updateCadence: quarterly signal scan and annual GAR refresh

reversibleResponses.action: Model critical dependency chains and run bounded tabletop failure sequences using public data
reversibleResponses.trigger: A dependency appears in multiple high-ranked risks or repeated disasters expose the same recovery bottleneck
reversibleResponses.rollback: Remove unverified dependencies and reset scenarios to the last reproducible model version
reversibleResponses.authorityBoundary: Automation owns public-data modeling and sandboxed exercises. Financial transactions, insurance decisions, emergency operations, and third-party coordination need separately classified authority; escalate only a substantiated nonautomatable barrier.

risks.title: Critical-infrastructure cyber compromise and latent dependency failure
risks.rankingRationale: Documented state-sponsored access to global networks can create correlated communications and service disruption. It is urgent and tractable for defensive monitoring, but this register has only a threat-cluster source and cannot infer global failure probability.

keyUnknowns: undetected persistence and concentration in shared suppliers
conversion of espionage access into destructive action
recovery performance under concurrent physical disruption

leadingIndicators.indicator: Verified advisories showing persistent access, exploitation of shared edge devices, or compromise across multiple infrastructure sectors
leadingIndicators.directionOfConcern: Broader affected sectors, longer dwell time, destructive tooling, or repeated failure to apply mitigations
leadingIndicators.updateCadence: weekly advisory scan and event-driven refresh

reversibleResponses.action: Maintain a non-secret dependency inventory template and run isolated recovery simulations against published indicators
reversibleResponses.trigger: A relevant verified advisory or discovery of an unmodeled single point of failure
reversibleResponses.rollback: Discard unverified indicators, isolate test artifacts, and restore the last known-good simulation baseline
reversibleResponses.authorityBoundary: Automation may use public advisories and isolated test environments. Scanning third-party systems, accessing credentials, changing production networks, or disclosing sensitive findings requires explicit bounded authority; human escalation is limited to a proven credential, consent, or legal barrier.

risks.title: Severe space weather disrupting power, navigation, communications, or spacecraft
risks.rankingRationale: Extreme geomagnetic events can produce correlated infrastructure stress, and the May 2024 G5 event demonstrates contemporary relevance. Lower frequency and useful warning systems reduce rank relative to persistent terrestrial risks.

keyUnknowns: actual failure propagation across modern interconnected infrastructure
operator response quality outside the exercise participants
severity and orientation of future Earth-directed solar events

leadingIndicators.indicator: NOAA watches and warnings, observed geomagnetic storm scale, and reported anomalies in grid, navigation, communications, or spacecraft systems
leadingIndicators.directionOfConcern: Earth-directed events forecast at severe or extreme levels with correlated system anomalies
leadingIndicators.updateCadence: daily automated public alert check and annual exercise review

reversibleResponses.action: Maintain a tested offline continuity checklist and simulate loss of time, navigation, communications, and grid dependencies
reversibleResponses.trigger: A severe NOAA watch or a newly identified unmitigated dependency
reversibleResponses.rollback: Restore the prior checklist and preserve simulation failures as evidence
reversibleResponses.authorityBoundary: Automation may monitor public alerts and run local simulations. Operational control of grids, radio, spacecraft, or emergency services remains outside scope and requires separately verified authorization; contact a human only for an irreducible owner-controlled action.

risks.title: Documentary, digital, and operational knowledge loss
risks.rankingRationale: Loss of records and recovery knowledge magnifies every other continuity risk and can be irreversible, but available evidence here is narrower and the program can take many low-risk reversible preservation steps.

keyUnknowns: global prevalence of untested disaster plans and inaccessible formats
concentration in fragile storage, vendors, credentials, or tacit expertise
whether backups can be independently restored under degraded conditions

leadingIndicators.indicator: Documented collections without tested disaster plans, independent fixity checks, format migration, geographically separated copies, or recovery exercises
leadingIndicators.directionOfConcern: Growing untested collections, repeated disaster exposure, inaccessible formats, or failed restoration tests
leadingIndicators.updateCadence: quarterly preservation review and after material storage changes

reversibleResponses.action: Inventory public and repository knowledge dependencies, verify local restoration in isolation, and record missing ownership
reversibleResponses.trigger: A failed restore, missing provenance, unsupported format, single-copy dependency, or approaching media end-of-life
reversibleResponses.rollback: Preserve source media unchanged, revert catalog mutations, and restore the last verified manifest
reversibleResponses.authorityBoundary: Automation may inspect in-scope public or repository artifacts and run nondestructive local recovery tests. Restricted archives, third-party data, credentialed storage, destructive migration, or physical custody changes require separate authorization; escalate to a human only when access or custody is demonstrably nonautomatable.
